science.title: The faintest supernova ever observed refuses to go out, staying visible for nearly a year
science.description: An international team of astronomers, including Paul Groot of Radboud University, has discovered that a supernova explosion does not always have to be extremely bright. The team has identified the faintest supernova observed to date. It remained visible for an exceptionally long time and appears to have been caused by a so-called white dwarf and a relatively small companion star. The discovery may have implications for our understanding of the evolution of binary stars and the measurement of the expansion of the universe. The results were published in Nature Astronomy.
